title: AdaptReg: Skip-level FiLM Adapter for Task-Specific Adaptation of a Frozen Registration Foundation Model
authors: Shuyue Shi; Rong Yuan; Lin Tian
abstract: Longitudinal PSMA-PET/CT registration is a key step in assessing treatment response in prostate cancer, and it requires more than generic alignment accuracy: the deformation must preserve lesion volume, so that measured changes in metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis (TLG) reflect treatment response rather than registration artifacts. We propose AdaptReg, which adapts a frozen registration foundation model to such task-specific requirements through a lightweight trainable adapter branch with identity-preserving initialization. Keeping uniGradICON fully frozen, we apply FiLM-style per-voxel affine modulation ($γ$, $β$) to its decoder skip connections; the modulation is generated from anatomical semantic features of a frozen TotalSegmentator encoder and supervised by a lesion volume-preservation loss. On the official Codabench validation set (20 pairs), AdaptReg achieves DSC 0.7585, HD95 6.33 mm, MTV/TLG errors of 1.68%/2.11%, and 0.0022% non-diffeomorphic voxels, improving on the uniGradICON + instance optimization baseline by $+0.05$ DSC and reducing the MTV/TLG errors by 70.9%/67.7%. On the hidden official test set (160 pairs), AdaptReg achieves CT DSC 0.816, PET DSC 0.598, and MTV/TLG errors of 4.02%/3.46%, ranking fourth among 16 teams in the final PSMAReg evaluation. Code: https://github.com/shishuyue/AdaptReg

title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
authors: Zecheng Hao; Zihan Huang; Shenghao Xie; Jiyuan Zhang; Zhaofei Yu; Tiejun Huang
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (S-GSA) and Spiking Local-Gated Unit (S-LGU), which enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity. We integrate the aforementioned mechanisms and modules into AdaS-ViT, a test-time adaptive-routing architecture trained with a progressive spatio-temporal curriculum that stabilizes the co-adaptation of firing precision and routing masks. Extensive experiments across benchmarks spanning diverse data scales and modalities demonstrate that AdaS-ViT consistently achieves highly competitive performance. Notably, on ImageNet-1k it consumes only 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and attains an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32$\times$ to 72$\times$, operating in an economical inference regime and thereby pushing the energy-efficiency boundary further.

title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
authors: Changzhi Ai; Frank Abild-Pedersen; Johannes Voss
abstract: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (coordination-based models like the alpha-scheme). Here, we present AdsNet, an equivariant graph neural network that directly predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass, which operates on a local graph restricted only to adsorbate atoms and its immediate surface neighbors within a cutoff radius. This local graph formulation decouples computational complexity from total system size while encoding continuous geometric features (interatomic distances and directional vectors) enabling sensitivity to subtle variations in local bonding environments. AdsNet adopts a message-passing architecture with scalar and vector node features over multiple interaction layers. Trained on AdsTraj, a dataset of 33,920 density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates (H*, C*, O*, CO*, OH*, HOCO*), the model achieves an adsorption energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/A. Analytic forces obtained via automatic differentiation enable structure relaxation through a projected gradient descent algorithm with adaptive line search, eliminating entire geometry optimizations. Additionally, AdsNet uniquely decomposes predicted adsorption energies into contributions from individual atoms within the local adsorbate graph - an interpretability feature unattainable with conventional machine-learning potentials. AdsNet thus establishes an accurate, highly efficient, and interpretable framework for large-scale adsorption energy prediction and local interface relaxation across various material surfaces.

title: Advanced Alternative Data Analytics and Machine Learning for Financial Fraud Detection and ESG Disclosure Quality
authors: Sarita Agarwal; Amrita Tatia Karnawat
abstract: <jats:p>Financial fraud and poor ESG disclosure stem from the same source: asymmetric information beyond the reach of traditional structured data. This chapter investigates how advances in alternative data and machine learning enhance fraud detection and the analysis of ESG disclosure quality. Through a descriptive-analytical approach employing secondary data—global surveys of fraud, alternative-data markets, ESG divergence and benchmarking studies—it synthesises patterns of performance across supervised, deep, graph and natural language processing techniques. The chapter finds that alternative data and machine learning significantly improve detection rates and expose greenwashing, but face class imbalance, model explainability issues, rating divergence and governance challenges. Recommendations are proposed, and a future research agenda outlined.</jats:p>

title: Adversarial robustness of dental panoramic radiograph classifiers against gradient-based perturbations
authors: Wenya Long; Teng He; Yingjuan Xie
abstract: <jats:p>Introduction: Deep learning classifiers for dental radiographs are increasingly deployed, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations is unmeasured. Methods: A frozen ResNet-18 backbone and a linear head were trained on 182 annotated teeth from the DENTEX dataset and attacked with the fast gradient sign method and projected gradient descent at budgets from 1/255 to 16/255, comparing a baseline model, an adversarially trained model and a median-filter defense. Results: The baseline classified 63.6% of held-out teeth correctly. Both attacks flipped every correctly classified tooth at a budget of 1/255. The fast gradient sign method fell to 77.1% attack success at 16/255, whereas projected gradient descent remained at 100%. Neither adversarial training nor the median filter reduced attack success, and adversarial training lowered clean accuracy to 54.5%. Conclusions: A transfer-learning dental radiograph classifier with a frozen backbone and linear head is catastrophically vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, and the simple defenses tested do not restore robustness.</jats:p>

title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing
authors: Tianren Li; Dongbo Li; Hongkai Chen; Jie Liu; Guoliang Xing
abstract: Aerial sensing must combine uncertain overhead context with current observations while budgeting prediction, movement and image processing. AeroBelief uses the next executable action as the unit of verification against reference scores. It groups candidate views by first action, scans them with an inexpensive proposer, and selectively queries a structured world model (WM). Calibrated group bounds support strict commitment; a six-query controller connects selective prediction with belief updates, acceptance checks and scheduled sensing. Across four layout families, 40 worlds and 960 closed-loop executions, the AeroBelief controller completes 75.42% of tasks, compared with 73.33% for exhaustive WM scoring and 65.83% for line-of-sight geometry, using 91.81% fewer reference-candidate evaluations than exhaustive scoring. In fixed-reference replay with a six-query cap, proposer-scaled anchored bounds raised first-action certificate availability from 36.25% to 54.69% and reduced mean queries per state by 13.54% relative to unit-scale anchored bounds. A complete ground-hosted pipeline processes 2,685 self-collected 20-megapixel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images from seven DJI Mavic 3M routes. Context-guided admission and feedback retain all eight independently supported target confirmations with 76.05% fewer processed images and 70.02% less accumulated active processing service than uncapped all-frame processing; feedback saves another 5.17% of images relative to static context. The studies connect budgeted action selection with evidence-driven processing of recorded flight imagery.

title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
authors: Shiwei Wu; Yuwen Pan; Zhi Li; Yaowen Li; Yan Zhou; Xuemiao Xu; Yu Liu
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.

title: AesDistill: Distilling Generative Aesthetics for Image Color Enhancement
authors: Chuanzhi Xu; Chengkun Yue; Huiqi Liang; Haoyang Li; Zihan Deng; Qingwen Zeng; Pengfei Ye; Weidong Cai
abstract: Image color enhancement aims to improve visual appeal, but previous methods often learn to reproduce ground-truth expert targets. These targets reflect the preferences of a few experts and cover a limited range of aesthetic choices. Matching them does not ensure stronger aesthetic quality across different tastes and scenes. By contrast, large generative models learn rich visual knowledge from large image collections and often produce vivid, appealing image edits. However, direct generation can change the source image's semantic structure along with its colors. In this paper, we introduce AesDistill, a framework for distilling generative aesthetics into image color enhancement. We use 4 leading open-source large generative models to produce 64,644 edited images as teacher targets at a cost of about 3,360 H100 GPU-hours, forming the AesDistill Dataset. AesDistill also includes AesDistill Student, a 1.13M-parameter model that learns teacher color changes through confidence-weighted supervision while preserving the source image's semantic structure. We evaluate AesDistill with 12 aesthetic and 4 image-quality assessment models. Every teacher's targets rank above the FiveK and PPR10K expert target means in the joint assessment. Across both datasets, AesDistill Student outperforms all 20 baseline methods and ranks directly behind the 4 teachers. These results demonstrate that distilling aesthetics from generative models enables a compact student to outperform methods trained on expert targets.

title: A Fast, Programmable GPU-to-CPU Invocation Layer for GPU-Initiated Communication
authors: Jiakun Yan; Shiksha Patel; David Sidler; Gengyu Rao; Brandon Potter; Bradford Beckmann
abstract:
Modern GPU workloads increasingly rely on device-initiated communication to let GPU kernels communicate directly without synchronizing with the host at kernel boundaries. Existing libraries commonly favor placing transport control on GPU threads, an approach known as GPUDirect Async (GDA), and treat reverse offload to host proxy threads as a slower fallback. We argue that reverse offload can outperform GDA and should be a first-class communication path. We further propose exposing reverse offload as a programming interface that lets users define workload-specific communication operations.
  We present KIWI, a programmable reverse-offload framework that achieves sub-microsecond one-way device-to-host latency and hundreds of millions of operations per second. We address practical challenges of scaling reverse offload, including contention on shared queues, polling overhead, and load imbalance across proxies. KIWI-P2P, a SHMEM-like library built on KIWI, outperforms state-of-the-art GDA implementations in both latency and bandwidth. More importantly, KIWI-EP redesigns low-latency mixture-of-experts dispatch and combine kernels around workload-defined operations, lowering expert-parallel communication latency by up to 2.3x over the best existing backend on AMD GPUs and time per output token in vLLM by up to 29%. The source code of KIWI is available at https://github.com/AMDResearch/kiwi.

title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
authors: Haoran Ye; Tianrui Huo; Hangzhen Li; Xin Zhang; Guojie Song
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron's psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2--94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.

title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins
authors: Younghwan Joo; Jeonghoon Han; Sanghyun Oh; Soosik Bang; Sung-il Kim
abstract: Physics-based digital twins of air conditioning, a principal energy consumer in manufacturing and buildings, can be generated automatically from a declarative specification of its equipment, connections, and sizing. Large language models (LLMs) now write such specifications from plain-language descriptions. Evaluations of these specifications stop at parse success, completed runs, or textual similarity, and cannot reject a model that converges in simulation but is physically wrong. In this study, a four-level protocol is proposed that tests whether an LLM-written specification not only executes but also yields a physically valid digital twin. Each specification is executed through static validity, model build, simulation convergence, and behavioral equivalence with a hidden reference model within bands calibrated by $\pm$20% sizing perturbations. The protocol was applied to eight LLMs and fourteen HVAC topologies, five describing an existing low-humidity test chamber. To test for authorship bias, engineers and a second model family also described six topologies. Within three repairs, seven of eight models built in 98.6 to 100% of trials, with simulations converging in at least 80.0%, but reached behavioral equivalence in only 50.0 to 98.6%. About half of the failed trials converged, but not to the reference steady state, mostly in desiccant rotor systems. Pooled pass rates varied by under five percentage points across description authors. These results imply that the physics hardest to model in each field, here the desiccant rotor, must enter the generation framework as validation levels. The protocol can be adapted to other fields that generate executable digital twins from declarative specifications.

title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch
authors: Haoxuan Wang; Jianliang Ye; Sen Na
abstract: We study statistical inference for online sketched Newton methods, in which each Newton system is approximately solved by an inner randomized sketching solver. Existing work reveals a computational--statistical trade-off: the sketching solver (and its accelerated variants) reduces the per-step cost of Newton methods from $O(d^3)$ to $O(d^2)$, but the randomness introduced by sketching also inflates the limiting covariance of both the last and the averaged Newton iterates. In this work, we address this trade-off via gradient averaging. We show that simply replacing the stochastic gradient with a moving average at each step can mitigate, and in some cases eliminate, the trade-off in Newton sketch. Importantly, gradient averaging requires no additional oracle evaluations and leaves the contraction bound of the inner sketching solver unchanged. In particular, we prove that the last sketched Newton iterate with gradient averaging attains a limiting covariance no larger than that without gradient averaging, while the averaged iterate even attains the minimax optimal limiting covariance, matching that of the exact Newton method. To our knowledge, this is the first analysis showing that randomness introduced to improve computational efficiency need not compromise statistical efficiency as long as proper gradient estimates are used. The key analytical challenge is that gradient averaging destroys the crucial martingale difference structure underlying central limit theorem arguments. We overcome this challenge by analyzing the coupled two-timescale recursions governing the iterate and the gradient estimator. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression support our theoretical covariance comparisons.

title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
authors: Matthew L. Corbett
abstract: Current command and control (C2) platforms lack integrated simulation capabilities that would allow commanders to dynamically explore courses of action (COAs) during live operations. This paper presents ongoing research and contributions to the development of AGAMOTTO (Advanced Guidance and Analytics for Military Operations, Tactical Threats, and Outcomes) as part of the overarching NGC2 program, which advances the Army's efforts to modernize C2 systems, such as the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK). The paper outlines the current design, preliminary findings, and the remaining research tasks, with an emphasis on how the completed work will support tactical decision-making in future time-constrained environments. While the full system is still under development, initial development and results demonstrate the feasibility of AGAMOTTO. Early experiments highlight both the potential benefits and practical constraints of deploying AI-enabled tools in operational settings, and introduce lessons learned and a viable training strategy to make AI-generated COAs feasible in tactical scenarios.

title: AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
authors: Regina Carla Sousa; Denis Vargas; Elizabeth Wanner; Joshua Knowles
abstract: We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.

title: A Generative Model for Higher-Order Network Dynamics
authors: Valentina Sánchez; Theodore Papamarkou; Gonzalo Nápoles; Çiçek Güven; Koen V. Haak
abstract: Conventional network representations inferred from multivariate time series describe statistical relationships between pairs of components, even when the underlying dynamics involve group interactions that cannot be represented by pairwise interactions alone. Several multivariate information-theoretic measures have been proposed to characterise dependence beyond pairs. However, due to a lack of systems with known generating mechanisms, these measures have not been carefully validated or compared for empirical use. To address this, we here introduce a generative model of stochastic network dynamics with pairwise and higher-order interactions specified by the user. The higher-order interactions are represented by directed hyperedges, and the model provides a controlled benchmark for evaluating information-theoretic measures. Removing only the higher-order term gives a pairwise-only reference. The experiments test whether a measure detects changes induced by the higher-order term relative to this reference and recovers the participating nodes and their source-target roles. A separate experiment tests discrimination between a product coupling and a specified nonlinear pairwise control, with equal root-mean-square coupling magnitude under the pairwise-only reference. Several measures detected sufficiently strong higher-order interactions across the tested network topologies and coupling functions. In the separate discrimination experiment, the measures also separated the product coupling from the specified nonlinear pairwise control. Recovery, however, became harder as the number of candidate interactions grew. The framework therefore provides a testbed where the link between higher-order signatures and mechanisms can be tested, rather than assumed, before measures are applied to empirical data.

title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
authors: Jiahang Lin; Jiahao Chen; Yiding Wang; Shichun Liu; Chengjun Pan; Shihan Dou; Honglin Guo; Yuyang Hu; Changhao Jiang; Zhenhua Han; Hang Yan; Qi Zhang; Tao Gui; Xuanjing Huang
abstract: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns. (2) Team-based modification implements those requirements as generalizable changes rather than task-specific patches. (3) Requirement-driven selection merges a change only when it resolves a verified requirement and passes review. Empirically, on held-out tasks, AHE-Beta raises pass@1 from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than Base Harness, and achieves higher pass@1 than Claude Code, Meta-Harness, and AHE. In a blind human A/B test, real users prefer AHE-Beta in 31 of 48 valid pairs and rate it higher on all five dimensions, matching the directional preference of the user simulator. The human A/B results show that AHE-Beta achieves its goal of aligning harness evolution with real-world user requirements. Without further evolution, the gains transfer to GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with pass@1 improvements of 15.8% and 5.3% over Base Harness. Together, these results show that requirement-centered harness evolution is a more general method for improving agent capabilities.

title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
authors: Yiyang Du; Yuxuan Kuang; Qitao Zhao; Yixuan Wang; Zhanqiu Guo; Yi Xu; Xin Li; Wenbin He; Liu Ren; Chenyan Xiong
abstract: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
authors: Viet K. Nguyen; Mohammad I. Husain
abstract: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved model, tool, and system-prompt configurations, and enforces authorization through three policy checks. We implement ATI as an external security enforcement layer that integrates with existing agent frameworks without modifying their underlying models. We evaluate ATI in a simulated federation of eight organizations using six agent frameworks, each deploying a five-agent team. Security experiments involve two organizations and assess 14 attack scenarios and six benign tasks across five agent models, using five attack variations and three repetitions per variation. A panel of judge models evaluates the experimental outcomes. With all enforcement mechanisms enabled, attack containment increases from 43% to 84% (40% to 80% for the 11 attack scenarios evaluated consistently across all configurations), while enforcement introduces approximately 174 microseconds of overhead per request. ATI is released as an open-source, framework-independent package that uses IETF WIMSE workload token formats for identity and request verification and Entity Attestation Tokens for model, tool, and system-prompt integrity verification.

title: Agent Verifiers in Counterfactual Analysis: A Pilot Study Benchmarking Agentic Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
authors: Satiyabooshan Murugaboopathy; Entejar Alam; Adel Daoud; Connor T. Jerzak
abstract: Agents can expand the covariate space of randomized experiments by retrieving fast-moving local context missed by slow-changing survey baseline covariates, helping characterize who benefits most from an intervention. Verifying such covariates is difficult: individual treatment effects are unobserved, retrieval leakage can pull post-treatment information into nominally pretreatment summaries, and encoder leakage can inject post-treatment pretraining knowledge into representations even after temporal filtering of inputs. Guided by a two-channel information bound separating summary provenance from encoder weights, we propose a three-layer benchmark protocol: (i) retrieval admissibility via pre-treatment date filtering; (ii) heterogeneity validation scored rank-weighted average treatment effects (RATEs); and (iii) encoder admissibility checked with chronologically vintaged encoders, future-fact probes, and weight perturbations. Across 11 datasets anchored by Uganda's Youth Opportunities Program, we compare session-isolated retrieval (sandboxed, bounded-budget agent runs per study) against a persistent workspace teammate (xAI's GrokBot) that builds one date-verified corpus per study while blinded to outcomes. The workspace teammate yields higher mean RATE ratios in 6/11 datasets for text alone and 7 for combined features, though paired tests show neither workflow universally dominates. Even on fixed retrieved text, encoder choice significantly shifts heterogeneity signal. Chronologically vintaged probes show no clear evidence of weight leakage, but single-record adapter perturbation analyses show that memorized future facts, once present, persist until injected noise degrades model output. Temporal filtering of retrieval is necessary but insufficient: verifying agent-generated covariates requires jointly examining source provenance, out-of-sample treatment-effect signal, and encoder weights.

title: AggCLIP: Aggregating CLIP for Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection
authors: Zhi Li; Hanyu Wang; Fei Shen; Zhengtao Zhang
abstract: Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection (ZSMAD) aims to identify both appearance and geometric defects in novel categories without relying on target-specific training data, making it especially valuable in real-world scenarios constrained by data scarcity, privacy concerns, or high annotation costs. While recent approaches successfully adapt vision-language models like CLIP to achieve this open-vocabulary generalization, they still face significant challenges: (i) severe geometric information loss during 3D-to-2D point cloud rendering; (ii) spatially noisy 2D feature maps produced by raw CLIP patch embeddings, compounded by shallow late-stage modality fusion; and (iii) severe cross-modal semantic misalignment due to decoupled processing streams. To address these limitations, we propose AggCLIP, a novel framework that adapts frozen CLIP representations for ZSMAD by explicitly incorporating local geometric structure and visual spatial context. Specifically, to accurately localize fine-grained defects, we design a Geometry-Aware Spatial Aggregation (GSA) module that refines back-projected 3D point features via density-adaptive neighborhood weighting, alongside a Context-Aware Spatial Aggregation (CSA) module that smooths multi-scale 2D patch embeddings using a lightweight trainable adapter. Furthermore, to prevent semantic drift between modalities, we introduce a Dual-Stream Prompt Contrastive (DSPC) loss, which aligns the abstract concepts of normality and abnormality across the point cloud and RGB streams. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed AggCLIP framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies benchmarks under both one-vs-rest and cross-dataset zero-shot settings, notably surpassing the strongest competitive methods by up to 2.9% in pixel-level AUPRO.

title: Agreement Is Not Accuracy: LiDAR Elevation Errors Hidden in LiDAR-Camera Extrinsics
authors: Yeon Kun Lee; Dongseok Yang; Deok-Kyeong Jang; Choongho Chung; Junyoung Lee; Hyeongseok So
abstract: LiDAR and cameras provide complementary measurements for 3D vision, yet agreement between their observations does not establish the accuracy of either sensor's internal geometry. We show that systematic LiDAR elevation biases can be absorbed into the estimated extrinsics. Using synchronized LiDAR intensities and camera-estimated checkerboard poses, we jointly estimate a sensor-specific elevation correction shared across recordings and extrinsics for each recording. Ray-plane intersections locate the checker pattern without using reported ranges, preventing range errors from directly moving the lookup. Under matched intensity and correction models, this lookup gives smaller camera-consistency residuals than measured-point lookup. Across six identically designed rigs using the same sensor models, recording-excluded corrections reduce the mean translation-reference distance from 7.57 to 3.04 mm. On separate structures, they reduce inter-plane angle errors against references from independent dense camera scans and improve image-edge alignment. Rolling the rigs shifts the plane pairs exhibiting the largest angular improvements, as predicted for an elevation-only correction. Within the ray-plane model, calibration-target projections and loop-consistency residuals change little despite these geometric improvements. These findings show why agreement after extrinsic calibration need not establish correct internal LiDAR geometry. Synchronized observations of a familiar checkerboard provide a practical route to estimating and testing elevation corrections without a dedicated large calibration field. We plan to release code and data for reproducing the main results.

title: AGSR: Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution for Gaussian Splatting
authors: Ayman Alkhateeb; Hadi Amirpour; Christian Timmerer
abstract:
3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time novel view synthesis, but Gaussian rasterization attenuates fine-scale scene structure through the projected covariance of each primitive. We show that contracting these projected covariances at inference time can mitigate the effective bandwidth limitation induced by finite Gaussian footprints, motivating a multi-aperture rendering framework for super-resolution.
  Based on this insight, we propose AGSR (Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution), a lightweight inference-time framework that progressively fuses multi-aperture renderings using uncertainty-guided feature aggregation and geometric conditioning from transmittance and depth cues. AGSR operates as a plug-in enhancement for pre-trained 3DGS models.
  Experiments on the Mip-NeRF 360 benchmark show that AGSR outperforms lightweight image-space super-resolution baselines, with gains increasing as the underlying Gaussian representation deteriorates. The results provide evidence that covariance contraction exposes bandwidth-sensitive structural cues attenuated by native Gaussian rasterization. AGSR achieves these improvements while maintaining real-time performance with up to 139k parameters.

title: A Hardware-Aware Comprehensive Study of Edge Vision Deployment with A Unified Hardware-Model-Runtime Mapping Framework
authors: Le Duc An; Le Duc Thanh; Vo Hoai Viet
abstract: The rapid growth of deep learning has driven the deployment of computer vision directly on resource-constrained edge devices. However, the extreme heterogeneity of edge hardware architectures poses major challenges in selecting and designing suitable vision models. This survey bridges the gap between edge hardware constraints, model architectures, and deployment software toolchains. We establish a comprehensive taxonomy classifying edge hardware into three distinct tiers: mid-range devices (GPUs and dedicated NPUs or TPUs), dedicated embedded MPU or SoC processors, and microcontrollers (MCUs). We aggregate and analyze multi-source benchmark results for image classification and object detection across the computing spectrum, spanning from tens of watts down to milliwatt-scale bare-metal MCUs. Based on these empirical findings, we propose a two-tiered hardware-to-model mapping framework that provides concrete model selection matrices across performance priorities (Speed, Balanced, Accuracy) and actionable architectural design principles (peak SRAM budgeting, resolution-first scaling, and algorithm-compiler co-design). Finally, we highlight critical deployment challenges including toolchain fragmentation, operator incompatibility, and Vision Transformer feasibility, and outline promising future research directions in on-device adaptation and sustainable Edge AI.

title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
authors: Yuze Wu; Mo Zhu; Xingxing Li; Yuheng Du; Zhaoqi Wang; Yuxin Fan; Wenjun Li; Kenghou Hoi; Zhichao Han; Xin Zhou; Fei Gao
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are expected to achieve semantic reasoning, intelligent decision-making, and long-horizon navigation under strict onboard constraints. While recent foundation-model-driven approaches have shown promising progress toward this goal, existing methods remain limited by challenges in 3D data availability, trajectory feasibility, long-horizon reasoning, and computational efficiency in complex environments. To bridge these gaps, we propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation (VLN) framework for aerial robots. VLN-AR decouples multimodal reasoning and low-level control, enabling structured prediction of 3D pose commands and navigation intentions that are translated into dynamically feasible actions. To mitigate data scarcity and domain gaps, we introduce a fully automated 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based pipeline to generate scalable photorealistic UAV navigation data. A progressive three-stage training strategy further enhances grounding, scene reasoning, and complex navigation. In addition, a lightweight cognitive agent improves long-horizon reasoning via memory-aware task decomposition. Finally, we design onboard optimization techniques, including token sparsification and model lightweighting, achieving 7.1x-9.4x speedup while maintaining high navigation performance on resource-limited UAV platforms. Experiments show great improvements over existing methods in both simulation and real-world UAV navigation. Project website: https://wyz000.github.io/VLN-AR/

title: A Hybrid RAG Framework for Deceptive Review Detection: Integrating RoBERTa-LoRA, FAISS-Based Retrieval, and LLM Reasoning
authors: Andrei Kostin; José Ángel Diaz-Garcia; Karel Gutiérrez-Batista
abstract: The growth of deceptive online opinions poses a critical risk of misinformation and fraud. This paper proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to automatically distinguish spam reviews. The architecture integrates RoBERTa with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) classification, FAISS semantic vector retrieval, and a Large Language Model (LLM) for final reasoning. The system was evaluated across balanced and severely imbalanced real-world scenarios. Results demonstrate that five epochs of fine-tuning enable robust domain transfer, achieving an F1-score of 0.90 in cross-domain evaluation, outperforming baselines (OpenAI Detector,F1 = 0.82) and demonstrating competitive performance against specialized in-domain SOTA models (fakeRoBERTa,F1 = 0.97). The proposed architecture provides evidence-backed explainability and statistically significant precision gains while maintaining comparable overall detection performance.

title: AI Adoption, Well-Being, and Gender Among Indonesian Gen Z Workers
authors: Abiqail Yolanda; Ady Purnama
abstract: <jats:p>This study examines how AI adoption relates to Generation Z workers' psychological well-being. It is inspired by Social Exchange Theory (SET) and Conservation of Resources (COR) Theory, placing emotional intelligence (EI) and self-efficacy (SE) as predictors of AI adoption, AI adoption as a mediator between the two resources and well-being, and gender as a potential moderator between EI/SE and AI adoption. PLS-SEM was used to analyze Gen Z worker data. The effect of both EI and SE on the prediction of AI adoption is significant, with EI having the larger effect. The use of AI is a strong predictor of well-being and influences both resources. There was no significant moderation by sex for either pathway in this sample. The results of this study reveal that AI adoption is a crucial behavioral process employee well-being, and that AI can be integrated into the work processes, providing empirical evidence to support AI strategies that enhance employee mental health.</jats:p>

title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
authors: Alexandra Starostina; Alexander Hermann; Mahish Guru; Kartik Bali; Roland Aydin; Christian C. Cyron
abstract: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. Classical optimisers, Bayesian or derivative-free, need a person to cut the design down to a few parameters, and on all the values they need far more solves; industrial shape optimisers move every surface node of the mesh in one solve per cycle, but only in small steps that polish rather than redesign. We ask whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can meet all three by joining what it knows with what the simulation shows. GPT-6 Astra edits a magnesium stent through a CAD geometry parametrisation of about 1,650 values, with a budget of 15 simulations; every proposal is built in CAD, meshed and simulated with large-deformation plasticity and contact, and the LLM reads the full results of every solve. Within that budget it lowered the objective, a high percentile of the strains in the stent's bends, by 32%; on the same budget, the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped improving. An earlier GPT-6 Astra design, 25% lower in the same objective, was checked in an independent, higher-fidelity model of the full deployment with crimping and damage: it was 14% less strained than the original after the full chain, and its most damaged spot began to fail later and carried 63% less damage at full expansion. LLMs can thus join their learned knowledge with simulation data to adjust more than a thousand design values and reach valid designs with real improvements.

title: AI and Blockchain Convergence for IoT Risk Governance
authors: Rachmad Andri Atmoko; Citra Dewi Megawati; Akas Bagus Setiawan; Hendra Yufit Riskiawan; Ismail Rakip Karas
abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain can strengthen cybersecurity risk governance. AI supports anomaly detection, predictive analytics, threat intelligence processing, and automated response, while blockchain provides tamper-resistant records, data provenance, smart contract-based compliance, and auditable decision trails. The chapter proposes the AI-Blockchain Driven Risk Governance Model (ABRGM), a layered framework aligned with NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0. It explains how the model connects verified security data, explainable AI decisions, automated governance controls, and executive risk reporting. Sector examples from finance, healthcare, and critical infrastructure show how the convergence can improve resilience, accountability, and continuous compliance while addressing scalability, privacy, regulatory, and organizational challenges.</jats:p>

title: AI and the Evolution of Materiality in Sustainability Reporting
authors: Ivneet Kaur Walia; Aastha Tiwari; K. Ankita Rao
abstract: <jats:p>Materiality determines what information an organisation must disclose in financial and sustainability reporting. Traditionally, such assessments relied on human judgement and fixed thresholds. However, AI is reshaping this process by identifying patterns, risks and impacts that may remain unnoticed through conventional review. This is especially relevant to ESG reporting, where corporate discretion may lead to selective disclosure, omission, or greenwashing. This chapter examines AI's potential as a forensic tool for identifying inconsistencies, misleading claims and hidden sustainability risks. It also considers the risks of algorithmic bias, opacity and over-reliance on automated outputs. Using an interdisciplinary approach, the chapter connects accounting principles, and sustainability-reporting frameworks. It proposes a framework for AI-assisted materiality assessment that supports transparency and accountability while preserving meaningful human oversight.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Early Detection of Micronutrient Deficiencies in Athletes Using Facial and Tongue Imaging for Performance Optimization and Recovery Enhancement
authors: Khushi Mehndiratta; Khyati Verma; Geetanjali Babbar; Vishan kumar Gupta
abstract: <jats:p>Micronutrient deficiencies are underdiagnosed and have a significant negative impact on athletic performance, recovery, and long-term physiological health, yet they are detected through invasive biochemical measurements. This article introduces a non-invasive Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based system for early detection of micronutrient deficiencies by analyzing facial and tongue images. The framework is built around computer vision methods, transformer-based feature extraction (DINOv2), unsupervised clustering, and neural network classification for the detection of visual biomarkers like skin pallor, irregularities in texture, and tongue discoloration. A dual-feature face and tongue approach yields greater predictive accuracy. The system also gives personalized dietary advice based on the principles of precision nutrition. The proposed solution provides a scalable, cost-effective, and accessible way to continuously monitor athletes' nutrition and optimize performance.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Human Flow Analysis
authors: Mariusz Barczak; Michał Pawlak
abstract: <jats:p>AI-supported human flow analysis is becoming increasingly critical for optimizing operations, energy management, and safety across non-ticketed spaces. While the retail sector faces growing pressure to improve sustainability and operational efficiency, the tourism sector has unexpectedly emerged as an innovation environment for AI-based footfall analytics. Open, unstructured spaces- such as historical sites and outdoor attractions - require precise, privacy-preserving measurement of visitor volumes. This paper examines how solutions originating in tourism, including the TourSenseAI framework, can be adapted for retail applications. By leveraging Deep Learning (DL) for crowd counting and Edge Computing for real-time processing, this work proposes a prototype AI-powered monitoring device designed to enhance process efficiency in complex retail environments.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Risk Assessment in Forensic Accounting and ESG Reporting
authors: Mehak Jonjua
abstract: <jats:p>Combining AI with forensic accounting and ESG reporting has been one of the biggest developments in modern financial regulation. This research explores how AI can increase the accuracy of fraud detection, and improve the reliability and completeness of ESG disclosures, in light of the current limitations associated with traditional audit techniques and the piecemeal nature of sustainability frameworks. Based upon Institutional Theory, Dual-Process Theory, and Explainability and Accountability Theory, a mixed-methods approach using survey responses from 342 respondents, structural equation modelling, and interview data was used to analyze the effects of AI on organizational performance. AI governance adequacy was found to be the strongest predictor of performance; and the best way to deploy AI was determined to be a model of human-AI complementarity, rather than complete automation.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven and Blockchain-Enabled Anomaly Detection for Cyber Risk Assessment in Cloud-Edge IoT and Wireless Sensor Networks
authors: Rahul Mishra
abstract: <jats:p>Cloud-edge-integrated Internet of Things (IoT) and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are not only enhancing their capabilities but also fortifying critical services across sectors such as healthcare, energy, and smart cities. However, their distributed and resource-constrained nature creates a wide and dynamic cyber-attack surface. The security mechanisms used earlier to detect operational deviations struggle to provide timely, granular, and trustworthy insights, limiting their usefulness for systematic cyber risk assessment. In this chapter, we have proposed a framework that combines various state-of-the-art technologies not only to detect but also to ensure tamper-proof event storage. The proposed framework combines AI-driven anomaly detection with blockchain-enabled assurance mechanisms to support robust cyber risk assessment in cloud-edge IoT and WSN deployments. AI models operating at edge and cloud layers learn normal operational patterns, detect deviations in real time, and quantify risk. At the same time, blockchain is used to secure anomaly logs, model-relevant events, and response actions in an immutable, verifiable ledger. The framework is further augmented with explainable AI techniques, such as feature importance analysis and local explanation methods like SHAP and LIME. This ensures anomaly decisions are transparent and interpretable for security analysts, auditors, and other non-technical stakeholders. By coupling intelligent detection with tamper-resistant evidence and interpretable outputs, the chapter offers a governance-oriented approach that enhances the reliability, accountability, and auditability of cyber risk assessment in complex cloud-edge IoT and WSN ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Compliance Automation With Smart Contracts
authors: M R H Khan; Md Masud Rana; Mir Mehedi Rahman
abstract: <jats:p>Cloud security governance, multi-cloud platforms and fintech payments are among the fastest-growing areas of cloud technologies as financial organizations increasingly rely on cloud-based operations. Organizations encounter increasing governance and audit burdens while endeavoring to ensure security and satisfy compliance obligations like PCI DSS. In this study, we present different perspectives on cloud governance, compliance automation and audit challenges in fintech systems. Blockchain-based systems use decentralized and immutable ledger that stores data as linked records. The necessity of blockchain-based governance models is increasing due to rising cloud complexity, continuous updates, and growing audit expectations. We propose a governance-by-design model for Zero Trust cloud security that integrates smart contracts, blockchain audit trails, CSPM, and AI-driven risk analytics to secure cloud environments and improve compliance processes. The model is supported by measurable evaluation metrics and addresses risks such as smart contract vulnerabilities and AI-related errors.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Detection of Greenwashing in ESG Reporting Using NLP and Machine Learning
authors: N. Sathyanarayana; G. Srividhya; G. Laxmana Rao; Madireddi S. S. V. Sri Kumar; K. Vidhya
abstract: <jats:p>Environmental, social and governance reporting creates opportunities for accountability and misleading environmental communication. This conceptual chapter examines how natural language processing and machine learning can support forensic scrutiny of sustainability disclosures. A critical literature review distinguishes textual classification, claim verification and professional findings. The proposed seven-layer framework connects document acquisition, structured extraction, linguistic analysis, numerical consistency testing, risk prioritisation, forensic validation and reporting. A worked application to Microsoft's public sustainability disclosure illustrates how reporting boundaries and relative measures affect interpretation. Current reporting and assurance developments, including ISSA 5000, inform the practical context. The framework offers an auditable decision process; its detection performance and assurance benefits require empirical validation.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Maximum Power Point Tracking in Solar Photovoltaic Systems
authors: Saurabh Pandey
abstract: <jats:p>Under variable environmental conditions, maximizing power obtained from a solar PV (SPV) system is fundamental, and for this purpose, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is required. This article presents a review of the artificial intelligence (AI)-based MPPT techniques such as machine learning, artificial neural network, adaptive neuro-fuzzy system, deep learning, and metaheuristic optimization. The methods of improving global MPPT in complex and partial shading conditions are studied for particle swarm optimization, grey wolf optimization, evolutionary algorithms, and hybrid intelligent-control techniques. The key performance measures such as tracking efficiency, convergence speed, oscillations, computational complexity, robustness, and real-time implementation are discussed. Challenges and directions for future development within adaptive learning, edge intelligence, explainable AI, and digital twins are emphasized.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Carbon-Aware Replenishment for Retail and Manufacturing
authors: Ural Gökay Çiçekli; Ewelina Idziak; Murat Kocamaz
abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops a reproducible carbon-aware replenishment framework linking data-driven demand forecasting to operational and proxy-based environmental outcomes in retail and manufacturing. Using the UCI Online Retail dataset, daily demand is forecast with a managerial baseline, the 7-day moving average, and an interpretable data-driven OLS model based on lagged demand and calendar effects. Forecasts are embedded into a single-echelon order-up-to replenishment simulation under fixed lead time and lost sales assumptions. Results show that the OLS-based model improves MAPE from 35.14% to 27.25% and reduces average inventory, total replenishment volume, waste-risk exposure, and proxy-based Scope 2 CO2e estimates across all tested EI/EF scenarios. However, service performance does not improve automatically, as fill rate declines under unchanged policy settings. The findings show that environmental and operational benefits from data-driven forecasting depend not only on better forecasts, but also on replenishment policy recalibration, bias monitoring, and transparent governance.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Digital Forensics and Data Integrity in Smart Microbiology Laboratories
authors: Amina Habib; Muhammad Umar Riaz; Muhammad Talha Ijaz; Anam Hanif; Um-e-Roman Nadeem; Bilal Ahmad; Muhammad Hassan; Sabira Sultana; Abu Sulman; Adnan Afzal; Babar Khan
abstract: <jats:p>The clinical microbiology laboratory is shifting from traditional culture-based, manual systems to automated, AI-driven smart laboratories. These platforms use real-time sensors, computer vision, and advanced algorithms to reduce human error, speed up workflows, and cut turnaround times significantly. Machine and deep learning models achieve over 95% accuracy in pathogen detection and can predict antimicrobial resistance using genomic, proteomic, or phenotypic data, supporting targeted therapy and stewardship. Data integrity is maintained through regulatory compliance, audit trails, and AI-based quality control, while privacy is protected using federated learning and encryption. Ethical oversight, regulation, and interdisciplinary collaboration remain essential.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Forensic Detection of Narrative Greenwashing in Sustainability Reports
authors: Shivani Naik; Sarvottam Rege
abstract: <jats:p>Sustainability reports for oil and gas corporations have ballooned to hundreds of pages. This study observes ten oil, gas, and energy companies that published official environmental disclosure and applies a reproducible set of tools word-frequency and keyword-in-context analysis, readability scoring, numeric-density and assurance-language checks, year-on-year cross-tabulation to analyze their reports, ESG data books, ratings, and/or regulatory filings. Research finds six cross-cutting patterns. Scope 3 emissions and what they actually comprise are missing consistently in half the reports. Headline “reduction” figures are context-free and base years vary. Market-based versus location-based emissions vary up to 47-fold with no indication which or both are reported. Narratives trump numbers when it comes to renewable energy. It is uncertain that the gaps reflect intent. All the figures are company-published and guaranteed true. But notice that the gaps recur across formats, auditors, and countries, and in most cases, the faults show when you read carefully and do basic arithmetic.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Forensic ESG Reporting and Corporate Accountability for Greenwashing in India and the United States
authors: Abhilash Aggarwal; Mehvish Mehraj
abstract: <jats:p>Machine-learning classifiers, natural language processing systems, and knowledge-graph ‎architectures are now identifying, at a scale that no conventional audit can manage, statistical and textual patterns associated with greenwashing. This chapter assesses whether AI-generated inconsistency detection could ‎result in corporate liability under Indian and United States law, and argues that it could, but ‎only through evidential pathways that neither system has yet tested. India has deliberately ‎designed its BRSR Core disclosure framework, coupled with its 2024 CCPA greenwashing ‎guidelines and the under-use of the PFUTP Regulations, to create a better infrastructure for ‎algorithmic verification. It is also a formalised evidential one by virtue of the Bharatiya ‎Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023's dual-certificate structure. The technical stages common to both systems are separated from the ‎jurisdictionally specific certification and liability-attribution stages that follow.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Green Technology Integration in Tourism Dimensions
authors: Atorika Lamare; Aman Kumar
abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the integrative role of AI-enabled green technologies in shaping sustainable development within rural tourism ecosystems through case based study in rural Meghalaya. It conceptualizes the interlinkages between intelligent technological adoption and key tourism dimensions, economic viability, environmental stewardship, socio-cultural preservation, and experiential enhancement. The analysis posits that AI-driven systems, including predictive analytics, smart resource management, and real-time monitoring, facilitate efficient resource utilization while mitigating ecological degradation. Simultaneously, these technologies enhance tourism competitiveness through personalization, demand forecasting, and operational optimization. However, the adoption process is constrained by infrastructural deficits, financial limitations, skill gaps, and governance complexities prevalent in rural contexts. The study further emphasizes the necessity of participatory governance, ethical AI deployment, and capacity-building mechanisms to ensure inclusive and equitable outcomes.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Neurotechnology and Brain-Computer Interfaces for Precision Living
authors: Olfa Rebai
abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI), neurotechnology, and brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) are reshaping personalized healthcare beyond traditional precision medicine. This chapter explores AI-enabled precision living as an emerging paradigm integrating neural, physiological, behavioral, and contextual information to support personalized cognitive wellness and adaptive healthcare. It reviews advances in neurotechnology, BCI systems, AI-based neural signal processing, and neuroadaptive applications, while introducing the AI-enabled Neurotechnological Precision Living (ANPL) framework. The framework connects multimodal data acquisition, intelligent state estimation, personalized prediction, adaptive intervention, and continuous learning with human well-being. Ethical, privacy, safety, equity, and governance challenges are also examined, highlighting the need for responsible, human-centered development of neuroadaptive health ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Precision Living and Personalized Wellness
authors: Yamijala Suryanarayana Murthy; Rohit Bansal; Mostafa Mohamad; Nishita Pruthi; Golli Mohan
abstract: <jats:p>The future of health management is being revolutionized by AI, predictive analytics, wearables, IoMT and digital health ecosystems. Traditional health care is reactive and disjointed, reacting to disease. Precision living with AI highlights real-time health monitoring, predictive risk assessment and personalised treatments. Many users receive personalised recommendations about how to live better and longer thanks to wearable intelligence, powerful data analysis and flawless digital health solutions. In this chapter a conceptual paradigm is proposed for personalised wellness experiences and perpetual health optimising with intelligent technology. It tackles key issues such as ethical governance of AI, digital inclusion, privacy and transparency of algorithms. The chapter discusses the need for future health care ecosystems to transform from episodic health care to intelligent, preventive and personalized environments for wellbeing that continuously foster human flourishing and sustainable health outcomes and improve quality of life.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Well-Being
authors: Artun Gacar
abstract: <jats:p>In this study, the effects of doomscrolling behavior—driven by artificial intelligence algorithms operating in the background of social media platforms—and empathetic artificial intelligence systems on digital well-being are comparatively examined through the content analysis method. The negative impact generated by doomscrolling behavior is addressed through viewer comments on the BBC's YouTube channel regarding the Molly Russell case ; meanwhile, the positive influence of empathetic artificial intelligence on digital well-being is investigated through user reviews of Wysa, an AI-powered therapy application. The findings demonstrate that algorithms can create positive or negative effects depending on their intended purpose and structure; therefore, the necessity of ethical, transparent, and user-centric design principles for ensuring digital well-being is emphasized.</jats:p>

title: AI-Green Last-Mile Delivery in Emerging Economies
authors: R. Alamelu; R. Purushothaman; M. Sathya; J. Leema Christina; I. Blessy Milca
abstract: <jats:p>The rapid expansion of e-commerce in the emerging markets of India, Africa, and Southeast Asia has put the last-mile delivery (LMD) systems at a greater strain to be made faster, more cost-efficient, and environmentally friendly. Despite the growing popularity of AI-based green technology as the transformative agent in the retail and manufacturing logistics, and it is limited by the infrastructural inadequacies, institutional inspections, and the digital maturity levels. This chapter examines the key barriers to integrating AI-powered green last-mile delivery in the emerging economies and evaluates the causal correlation using Fuzzy DEMATEL and MICMAC analysis. Using case evidence of logistics and e-commerce organisations in service in India and similar markets, the study has found infrastructural preparedness, technological capability, and regulatory consistency to be the most important driver variables. It presents a systematic and evidence-based roadmap to implementing AI-powered green delivery solutions that consider efficiencies and sustainability objectives.</jats:p>

title: AIoT-Driven Intelligent Detection and Mitigation Support for Non-Technical Losses in Smart Grids
authors: Francisco R. Trejo-Macotela
abstract: <jats:p>Electricity theft, a non-technical loss, remains a persistent utility problem. This chapter proposes a three-tier Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) architecture linking device acquisition, edge screening, cloud analysis and human-supervised decision support. An offline component-level experiment used a versioned State Grid Corporation of China dataset and a stratified holdout of 8,474 consumers to compare five central models and a simulated distributed Random-Forest tree pool. XGBoost achieved the highest F1, 0.3717 (95% bootstrap CI [0.3449, 0.3962]), AUC-ROC, 0.7752 [0.7556, 0.7922], and MCC, 0.3080 [0.2772, 0.3362]; Random Forest had the highest recall, 0.5208 [0.4861, 0.5540]. At threshold 0.50, XGBoost detected 339 of 722 theft-labelled consumers and missed 383. The tree pool reached F1 = 0.3347 and AUC-ROC = 0.7685, but is neither FedAvg nor a formal privacy mechanism. Missing consumption cells comprised 25.64%. Results support model comparison and future design, not field validation, end-to-end latency or loss-reduction claims, or automated enforcement.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Green Technology Integration in Retail Green Marketing
authors: Margarita Išoraitė
abstract: <jats:p>The chapter examines AI-powered green technology, green marketing, and AI-powered green technology integration in retail green marketing and analyzes a case study. The aim of the article is to assess the specifics of AI-powered green technology, green marketing, and AI-powered green technology integration in retail green marketing. The objectives of the article are to assess the AI-powered green technology, green marketing, and AI-powered green technology integration in the retail green marketing concept and evaluate AI-powered green technology integration in retail green marketing cases abroad and in Lithuania. The article used the methods of scientific literature analysis and case analysis. The analysis of important aspects, such as a process approach, holistic thinking, and benefits are seen in the definitions of AI-powered green technology, green marketing, and AI-powered green technology integration in retail.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Green Technology Integration in the Building Value Chain in Malaysia
authors: Sook Yen Lee; Chee Ann Lim; Mohd. Faiz Hilmi
abstract: <jats:p>AI is increasingly transforming the integration of green technologies. While existing studies primarily emphasise operational efficiency in manufacturing and retail, limited attention has been given to the role of AI in shaping consumer adoption of green technologies, particularly in high-value assets such as green buildings. This gap is especially evident in emerging economies such as Malaysia, where green building adoption remains constrained despite supportive policies. This chapter develops a conceptual framework that positions AI as an enabling mechanism linking production-side innovation with consumer decision-making within the building value chain. Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behaviour and housing economics, the framework explains how AI influences behavioural factors and economic expectations that shape green building adoption. The chapter highlights how AI enhances information transparency, reduces perceived risk and improves economic evaluation. The findings offer an AI-driven sustainable housing adoption models for key stakeholders in emerging economies.</jats:p>

title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
authors: Heeseung Shin; Changwon Lim
abstract: BraTS-GoAT Task 3 evaluates brain-tumor segmentation across heterogeneous entities using shared ET, TC, and WT regions. We present a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels, a training-only nested-region objective, and a four-expert bottleneck adapter. Five-fold ResEnc-M/L teachers gener ated predictions for 1,138 unlabeled cases; fusion, hierarchy enforcement, and confidence-and-agreement screening retained 983 for training with 1,351 annotated cases. The final five-fold ResEnc-M entry achieved mean DSC 0.834, mean NSD 0.510, and Acalc = 0.6720 on the validation server. Component effects were modest and region-dependent, with the clearest gains on ET. Source code is available at https://github.com/HeeSeung-Shin/Brats2026-Goat-HS.
